title: Choosing a flat Artinian subalgebra and elements of Lambda landing in it (the choice in the proof of Stacks 07FH)
statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, $\Lambda$ a Noetherian $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] geometrically regular over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], $\mathfrak q\subset\Lambda$ a prime ideal, $n\ge1$, and $\bar\Lambda=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q^n\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], a local ring with maximal ideal $\bar{\mathfrak m}=\mathfrak q\bar\Lambda$ and residue field $K=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. Call a $k$-subalgebra $A\subseteq\bar\Lambda$ *admissible* if $A$ is an Artinian local ring, essentially of finite type over $k$ (isomorphic as a $k$-algebra to a localization $S^{-1}B$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] of a finitely generated $k$-algebra $B$ at a multiplicative subset $S\subseteq B$), the inclusion $A\to\bar\Lambda$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and $\mathfrak m_A\bar\Lambda=\bar{\mathfrak m}$; then $\mathfrak m_A=A\cap\bar{\mathfrak m}$ and the residue field $F=A/\mathfrak m_A$ is a subfield of $K$ containing $k$. Let $A_0\subseteq\bar\Lambda$ be admissible. Then there are an admissible $A\subseteq\bar\Lambda$ with $A_0\subseteq A$, with residue field $F$, and elements $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_t\in\Lambda$ and $\lambda'_1,\dots,\lambda'_r\in\mathfrak q$ ($t,r\ge0$) such that: (a) the images of all $\lambda_j$ and $\lambda'_i$ in $\bar\Lambda$ lie in $A$ (so the residues $\bar\lambda_j\in K$ lie in $F$); (b) $\mathrm d\bar\lambda_1,\dots,\mathrm d\bar\lambda_t$ form a basis of the $F$-vector space $\Omega_{F/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]; (c) the images of $\lambda'_1,\dots,\lambda'_r$ in $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ generate the ideal $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$.

Stacks asserts these choices without argument, and for an arbitrary A they are impossible: Lambda=k[x,y], q=0, n=1, A=k(x/y) is admissible, but k[x,y] meets k(x/y) only in k, while Omega_{A/k} is nonzero; so A must be enlarged. Suggested proof (agent): take a_j in A_0 with d of their residues a basis of Omega_{F_0/k}, and generators b_i of m_{A_0} (n>=2; for n=1 take generators of q), write them as mu/s with a common s in Lambda minus q, and enlarge A_0 according to the residue alpha of s exactly as in the three cases of the proof of Lemma 07FI (alpha transcendental over F_0: A=A_0[s-bar] localized, add s to the lambda's; alpha algebraic: Q=p^e >= n with alpha^Q separable over F_0, a finite etale A over A_0 with residue field F_0(alpha^Q) containing s-bar^N, N a power of p, and use mu s^(N-1), whose differentials are alpha^N d(residue))

proof.text:
*Setup.* $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ and residue field $K$, and $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\cap\Lambda=\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; it is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Write $\pi:\Lambda	o\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}	o ar\Lambda$ and $x\mapsto\hat x$ for the residue map $ ar\Lambda	o K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local] $ ar\Lambda$ is an Artinian local ring with maximal ideal $ ar{\mathfrak m}=\mathfrak q ar\Lambda$, $ ar{\mathfrak m}^n=0$; the kernel of $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}	o ar\Lambda$ is $\mathfrak q^n\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\subseteq\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, so the preimage of $ ar{\mathfrak m}$ in $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$. Every element of $ ar\Lambda$ is the image of some $\mu/s$, $\mu\in\Lambda$, $s\in\Lambda\setminus\mathfrak q$, and $\pi(s)$ is a unit of $ ar\Lambda$ for $s
otin\mathfrak q$. As $k	o ar\Lambda$ is injective, $p\cdot1=0$ in $ ar\Lambda$ and in $K$. *The parenthetical claims of the statement.* Let $A\subseteq ar\Lambda$ be admissible. From $\mathfrak m_A ar\Lambda= ar{\mathfrak m}$ we get $\mathfrak m_A\subseteq A\cap ar{\mathfrak m}$, a proper ideal of $A$ ($1
otin ar{\mathfrak m}$), so $\mathfrak m_A=A\cap ar{\mathfrak m}$ by maximality; hence $F=A/\mathfrak m_A	o ar\Lambda/ ar{\mathfrak m}=K$ is injective, a $k$-algebra map, and we regard $F$ as a subfield of $K$ containing $k$. An element $x\in A$ with $\hat x
eq0$ lies outside $\mathfrak m_A$, hence is a unit of $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent] $A$ is Noetherian with nilpotent maximal ideal, and by [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-unique-prime] $\mathfrak m_A$ is its only prime.

proof.text: *The residue field $F_0$ of $A_0$ and the elements $a_j$.* $A_0$ is essentially of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]: $A_0\cong W^{-1}B$ with $B=k[g_1,\dots,g_u]$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Every element of $A_0$ is $b/w$ with $b,w\in B$, so its residue lies in the subfield of $F_0=A_0/\mathfrak m_{A_0}\subseteq K$ generated over $k$ by the residues of $g_1,\dots,g_u$: $F_0/k$ is a finitely generated field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. By [lem-weil-pbc-cartier-equality] $\Omega_{F_0/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] is a finite dimensional $F_0$-vector space; it is spanned by the $\mathrm dc$, $c\in F_0$, so this spanning set contains a basis $\mathrm dc_1,\dots,\mathrm dc_t$ ($t\ge0$). Choose $a_j\in A_0$ with $\hat a_j=c_j$ ($A_0\to F_0$ is surjective).

proof.text: *Generators.* If $n\ge2$: $A_0$ is Noetherian (step 1), so $\mathfrak m_{A_0}=(b_1,\dots,b_r)$ for some $b_i\in\mathfrak m_{A_0}$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; since $A_0$ is admissible, $b_1,\dots,b_r$ generate the ideal $\mathfrak m_{A_0}\bar\Lambda=\bar{\mathfrak m}$ of $\bar\Lambda$. If $n=1$: $\Lambda$ is Noetherian, so $\mathfrak q=(\lambda'_1,\dots,\lambda'_r)$ for some $\lambda'_i\in\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; their images generate $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, and since $\bar{\mathfrak m}=\mathfrak q\bar\Lambda=\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}=0$, $\pi(\lambda'_i)=0$ lies in every subring of $\bar\Lambda$: these $\lambda'_i$ satisfy (a) and (c) for every admissible $A$.

proof.text: *A common denominator.* By step 1 write $a_j$ ($j\le t$) and, if $n\ge2$, $b_i$ ($i\le r$) as images of fractions $\mu_j/s_j$, $\mu'_i/s'_i$ with $\mu_j,\mu'_i\in\Lambda$, $s_j,s'_i\in\Lambda\setminus\mathfrak q$; with $s=\prod_js_j\prod_is'_i\in\Lambda\setminus\mathfrak q$ ($\mathfrak q$ prime) and the numerators multiplied by the other denominators we get $s\in\Lambda\setminus\mathfrak q$ and $\mu_j,\mu'_i\in\Lambda$ with $\pi(\mu_j)=a_j\pi(s)$ and $\pi(\mu'_i)=b_i\pi(s)$. Since $b_i\pi(s)\in\bar{\mathfrak m}$, $\mu'_i/1$ lies in the preimage $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ of $\bar{\mathfrak m}$, so $\mu'_i\in\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\cap\Lambda=\mathfrak q$ (step 1). Put $\bar s=\pi(s)$, a unit of $\bar\Lambda$, and $\alpha=\hat{\bar s}\in K$, $\alpha\neq0$.

proof.text: *Claim (first part of the proof of 07FI).* Let $D_1\subseteq\bar\Lambda$ be a subring which is a local ring with $\mathfrak m_{D_1}=D_1\cap\bar{\mathfrak m}$, so that its residue field $F_1$ is a subfield of $K$, and let $x\in\bar\Lambda$ with $\hat x\in F_1\setminus\{0\}$. Then $x^q\in D_1$ for every power $q=p^e$ of $p$ with $q\ge n$. Proof: choose $y\in D_1$ with $\hat y=\hat x^{-1}$; then $y\notin\mathfrak m_{D_1}$, so $y$ is a unit of $D_1$, and $\varepsilon=yx-1\in\bar{\mathfrak m}$. As $p=0$ in $\bar\Lambda$, $(1+\varepsilon)^{p^e}=1+\varepsilon^{p^e}$ (induction on $e$), and $\varepsilon^q\in\bar{\mathfrak m}^q\subseteq\bar{\mathfrak m}^n=0$. So $(yx)^q=1$ and $x^q=(y^{-1})^q\in D_1$.

proof.text: *Two cases.* Either $\alpha$ is transcendental over $F_0$ (not a root of a nonzero polynomial with coefficients in $F_0$ [def-weil-algebraic-element]; case T, steps 7-9) or $\alpha$ is algebraic over $F_0$ (case S, steps 10-13). In each case we construct an admissible $A\supseteq A_0$ with residue field $F\subseteq K$ and a power $N\ge p$ of $p$ with $\bar s^N\in A$, such that in case T, $\bar s\in A$ and $\mathrm dc_1,\dots,\mathrm dc_t,\mathrm d\alpha$ is a basis of $\Omega_{F/k}$, and in case S, $\mathrm dc_1,\dots,\mathrm dc_t$ is a basis of $\Omega_{F/k}$ (here $\mathrm dc_j$ denotes $\mathrm d$ of $c_j\in F_0\subseteq F$ in $\Omega_{F/k}$).

proof.text: *Case T: the ring $D'$ (as in 07FI, case transcendental).* Let $\theta:A_0[t]\to\bar\Lambda$ be the $A_0$-algebra map with $t\mapsto\bar s$ and $\mathfrak n=\theta^{-1}(\bar{\mathfrak m})$. Since $A_0\subseteq\bar\Lambda$ is local, $\mathfrak m_{A_0}[t]\subseteq\mathfrak n$, and modulo $\mathfrak m_{A_0}[t]$ the map $A_0[t]\to K$ is $F_0[t]\to K$, $t\mapsto\alpha$, which is injective as $\alpha$ is transcendental over $F_0$; so $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m_{A_0}[t]$, a prime ideal ($A_0[t]/\mathfrak n=F_0[t]$ is a domain). Let $D'=A_0[t]_{\mathfrak n}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. $A_0[t]$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] and so is $D'$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. $D'/\mathfrak m_{A_0}D'=(F_0[t])_{(0)}=F_0(t)$ is a field and $\mathfrak m_{A_0}D'$ is nilpotent ($\mathfrak m_{A_0}$ is, step 1), so $\mathfrak m_{A_0}D'$ lies in every prime of $D'$ and is the maximal ideal of the local ring $D'$; $D'$ is Artinian local [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local] (with $K=0$ there), with residue field $F_0(t)$, and $A_0\to D'$ is local. Every element of $A_0[t]\setminus\mathfrak n$ maps outside $\bar{\mathfrak m}$, i.e. to a unit of $\bar\Lambda$, so $\theta$ extends to $\psi':D'\to\bar\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], local ($\psi'^{-1}(\bar{\mathfrak m})=\mathfrak nD'$), restricting to the inclusion on $A_0$, with $\psi'(t/1)=\bar s$; on residue fields it is $F_0(t)\to K$, $t\mapsto\alpha$.

proof.text: *Case T: $A=\psi'(D')$ is admissible.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-criterion-flatness-fibre-noetherian] to $R=A_0$, $S=D'$, $S'=M=\bar\Lambda$: Noetherian local rings (steps 1, 7) and local homomorphisms; $M$ is generated by $1$ and nonzero; $M/\mathfrak m_{A_0}M$ is a vector space over the field $D'/\mathfrak m_{A_0}D'$, hence free and flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; $M$ is flat over $A_0$ ($A_0$ admissible). So $\psi'$ is flat; being local it is faithfully flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat] and so injective [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] ($I=0$). Let $A=\psi'(D')\cong D'$, a $k$-subalgebra of $\bar\Lambda$ containing $A_0=\psi'(A_0)$ and $\bar s$: it is Artinian local, $A\to\bar\Lambda$ is flat, and $\mathfrak m_A\bar\Lambda=\mathfrak m_{A_0}\bar\Lambda=\bar{\mathfrak m}$. Its residue field $F\subseteq K$ is the image of $F_0(t)$, i.e. $F=F_0(\alpha)\cong F_0(t)$ ($t\mapsto\alpha$), finitely generated over $k$ (by $\alpha$ and generators of $F_0$, step 2). Writing $F=k(e_1,\dots,e_v)$, $F=W^{-1}k[e_1,\dots,e_v]$ with $W$ the nonzero elements of the domain $k[e_1,\dots,e_v]$, so $k\to F$ is essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra] [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and by [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-essentially-finite-type-residue] $A$ is essentially of finite type over $k$. So $A$ is admissible, $A_0\subseteq A$, $\bar s\in A$; put $N=p$ (then $\bar s^N\in A$).

proof.text: *Case T: a basis of $\Omega_{F/k}$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-polynomial-extension] ($R=k$, $A=F_0$, $e=1$) $\Omega_{F_0[t]/k}\cong(F_0[t]\otimes_{F_0}\Omega_{F_0/k})\oplus F_0[t]\,\mathrm dt$ via $b\otimes\mathrm dc\mapsto b\,\mathrm dc$; as $\mathrm dc_1,\dots,\mathrm dc_t$ is an $F_0$-basis of $\Omega_{F_0/k}$ (step 2), $\mathrm dc_1,\dots,\mathrm dc_t,\mathrm dt$ is an $F_0[t]$-basis of $\Omega_{F_0[t]/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. $F_0(t)$ is the localization of $F_0[t]$ at its nonzero elements, so by [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] $\Omega_{F_0(t)/k}$ is the localization of $\Omega_{F_0[t]/k}$ and $\mathrm dc_1,\dots,\mathrm dc_t,\mathrm dt$ is an $F_0(t)$-basis of it. Transporting along the $k$-algebra isomorphism $F_0(t)\cong F$, $t\mapsto\alpha$, identity on $F_0$ (step 8), $\mathrm dc_1,\dots,\mathrm dc_t,\mathrm d\alpha$ is an $F$-basis of $\Omega_{F/k}$.

proof.text: *Case S: the field $F_1=F_0(\beta)$ (as in 07FI, case algebraic).* $\alpha$ is algebraic over $F_0$, so $F_0(\alpha)/F_0$ is an algebraic extension and by [lem-weil-pbc-separable-first-purely-inseparable] there is $Q=p^e$ ($e\ge0$) with $\beta:=\alpha^Q$ separable over $F_0$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]; $\beta\neq0$. Let $F_1=F_0(\beta)\subseteq K$; it is generated by $\beta$, so $F_1\cong F_0[T]/(\bar g)$, $\bar g$ the minimal polynomial of $\beta$, is finite over $F_0$, and as the elements of $F_1$ separable over $F_0$ form a subfield containing $F_0$ and $\beta$ [lem-weil-pbc-separable-first-purely-inseparable], $F_1/F_0$ is finite and separable algebraic. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}F_1\to\operatorname{Spec}F_0$ is etale [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale]. $A_0$ and $\bar\Lambda$ are local rings whose only prime is the maximal ideal [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-unique-prime], hence henselian [lem-weil-pbc-local-dimension-zero-henselian]. By the essential surjectivity in [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-finite-etale-equivalence] for $A_0$ and the finite etale $F_0$-algebra $F_1$ there is a finite etale $A_0$-algebra $D'$ with an $F_0$-algebra isomorphism $D'/\mathfrak m_{A_0}D'\cong F_1$. $D'$ is finite over $A_0$, hence Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]; $\mathfrak m_{A_0}D'$ is nilpotent with quotient a field, so it is the maximal ideal of the local ring $D'$, which is Artinian [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local] with residue field $F_1$, and $A_0\to D'$ is local.

proof.text: *Case S: a factorization $A_0\to D'\to\bar\Lambda$ (Stacks: 'since $\bar\Lambda$ is henselian and $F(\alpha^q)$ is contained in its residue field we can find a factorization').* Let $\rho:D'\to F_1\subseteq K$ be the residue map composed with the isomorphism of step 10; on $A_0$ it is the residue map $A_0\to F_0\subseteq K$. Let $B=D'\otimes_{A_0}\bar\Lambda$; $\bar\Lambda\to B$, $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, is etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change]. The maps $\rho$ and $x\mapsto\hat x$ are ring maps $D'\to K$, $\bar\Lambda\to K$ agreeing on $A_0$, so they define a ring map $\chi:B\to K$, $d\otimes x\mapsto\rho(d)\hat x$, surjective (already on $1\otimes\bar\Lambda$). Its kernel $\mathfrak q'$ is a prime of $B$ lying over $\bar{\mathfrak m}$, and $K=\bar\Lambda/\bar{\mathfrak m}\to B/\mathfrak q'\cong K$ is the identity, an isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-etale-retraction] ($\bar\Lambda$ henselian, step 10) there is a $\bar\Lambda$-algebra map $\sigma:B\to\bar\Lambda$ with $\sigma^{-1}(\bar{\mathfrak m})=\mathfrak q'$. Put $\psi'(d)=\sigma(d\otimes1)$. For $a\in A_0$, $\psi'(a)=\sigma(1\otimes a)=a$, so $\psi'$ restricts to the inclusion on $A_0$. Reducing $\sigma$ modulo $\bar{\mathfrak m}$ gives a $K$-algebra map $B/\mathfrak q'\to K$, which is the inverse of the isomorphism $K\to B/\mathfrak q'$; hence $\widehat{\psi'(d)}=\chi(d\otimes1)=\rho(d)$ for $d\in D'$. So $\psi'$ is local ($\psi'^{-1}(\bar{\mathfrak m})$ is a prime of $D'$, i.e. $\mathfrak m_{A_0}D'$, by [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-unique-prime]) and induces on residue fields the inclusion $F_1\subseteq K$.

proof.text: *Case S: $A=\psi'(D')$ is admissible and $\bar s^N\in A$.* As in step 8, [lem-weil-pbc-criterion-flatness-fibre-noetherian] for $A_0\to D'\to\bar\Lambda$ and $M=\bar\Lambda$ ($M/\mathfrak m_{A_0}M$ is a vector space over the field $D'/\mathfrak m_{A_0}D'\cong F_1$, hence flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; $M$ flat over $A_0$) shows that $\psi'$ is flat; it is local, hence faithfully flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat] and injective [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction]. $A=\psi'(D')\cong D'$ is a $k$-subalgebra of $\bar\Lambda$ containing $A_0$, Artinian local, flat into $\bar\Lambda$, with $\mathfrak m_A\bar\Lambda=\mathfrak m_{A_0}\bar\Lambda=\bar{\mathfrak m}$ and residue field $F=F_1=F_0(\beta)\subseteq K$ (step 11), finitely generated over $k$; as in step 8, $k\to F$ is essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra] [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and so is $k\to A$ [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-essentially-finite-type-residue]. So $A$ is admissible and $A_0\subseteq A$. By the Claim (step 5) for $D_1=A$ (local with $\mathfrak m_A=A\cap\bar{\mathfrak m}$, step 1) and $x=\bar s^Q$, whose residue $\beta\in F$ is nonzero, $\bar s^{Qq'}\in A$ for a power $q'$ of $p$ with $q'\ge\max(n,p)$. Put $N=Qq'$, a power of $p$ with $N\ge p$.

proof.text: *Case S: a basis of $\Omega_{F/k}$.* $F/F_0$ is finite separable (step 10), so $\operatorname{Spec}F\to\operatorname{Spec}F_0$ is etale [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale], i.e. $H_1(L_{F/F_0})=0$ and $\Omega_{F/F_0}=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine]. The Jacobi-Zariski sequence [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-homology-sequence] for $k\to F_0\to F$ contains the exact piece $H_1(L_{F/F_0})\xrightarrow{\partial}F\otimes_{F_0}\Omega_{F_0/k}\xrightarrow{w}\Omega_{F/k}\xrightarrow{z}\Omega_{F/F_0}\to0$, with $w(c\otimes\mathrm db)=c\,\mathrm db$; so $w$ is an isomorphism. Since $\mathrm dc_1,\dots,\mathrm dc_t$ is an $F_0$-basis of $\Omega_{F_0/k}$ (step 2), $1\otimes\mathrm dc_j$ is an $F$-basis of $F\otimes_{F_0}\Omega_{F_0/k}$, and its image $\mathrm dc_1,\dots,\mathrm dc_t$ is an $F$-basis of $\Omega_{F/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials].

proof.text: *The elements $\lambda_j$ and (a), (b).* In both cases let $A$, $F$, $N$ be as constructed (steps 8, 12). Put $\lambda_j=\mu_js^{N-1}\in\Lambda$ for $j=1,\dots,t$, and in case T also $\lambda_{t+1}=s$ (so the number of $\lambda$'s is $t$ in case S and $t+1$ in case T). By step 4, $\pi(\lambda_j)=a_j\bar s\,\bar s^{N-1}=a_j\bar s^N\in A$ ($a_j\in A_0\subseteq A$, $\bar s^N\in A$), and in case T $\pi(s)=\bar s\in A$. The residues are $c_j\alpha^N$ and, in case T, $\alpha$; here $\alpha^N=\widehat{\bar s^N}\in F\setminus\{0\}$. By the Leibniz rule in $\Omega_{F/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], $\mathrm d(c_j\alpha^N)=\alpha^N\mathrm dc_j+Nc_j\alpha^{N-1}\mathrm d\alpha=\alpha^N\mathrm dc_j$, since $p\mid N$ and $p=0$ in $F$ (in case S, $\alpha^{N-1}$ need not lie in $F$, but $N\alpha^{N-1}\mathrm d\alpha$ is not needed: write $c_j\alpha^N$ as $c_j\cdot\gamma$ with $\gamma=\alpha^N\in F$ and $\gamma=(\alpha^Q)^{q'}=\beta^{q'}$, so $\mathrm d\gamma=q'\beta^{q'-1}\mathrm d\beta=0$ as $p\mid q'$; in case T likewise $\gamma=\alpha^p$, $\mathrm d\gamma=p\alpha^{p-1}\mathrm d\alpha=0$). Hence the differentials of the residues are $\alpha^N\mathrm dc_1,\dots,\alpha^N\mathrm dc_t$ in case S, a basis of $\Omega_{F/k}$ by step 13 ($\alpha^N\in F^\times$), and $\alpha^N\mathrm dc_1,\dots,\alpha^N\mathrm dc_t,\mathrm d\alpha$ in case T, a basis by step 9. This proves (a) and (b) for the $\lambda$'s.

proof.text: *The elements $\lambda'_i$ and (a), (c).* For $n=1$ take the $\lambda'_i$ of step 3. For $n\ge2$ put $\lambda'_i=\mu'_is^{N-1}$ ($i=1,\dots,r$); $\lambda'_i\in\mathfrak q$ as $\mu'_i\in\mathfrak q$ (step 4), and $\pi(\lambda'_i)=b_i\bar s^N\in A$ (a). Let $J\subseteq\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ be the ideal generated by the images of the $\lambda'_i$. Its image in $\bar\Lambda$ is generated by the $b_i\bar s^N$, which generate $\bar{\mathfrak m}$ (step 3; $\bar s$ is a unit); as $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is the preimage of $\bar{\mathfrak m}$ and contains the kernel $\mathfrak q^n\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ (step 1), $J+\mathfrak q^n\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, so, as $n\ge2$, $J+(\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q})\cdot(\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q})=\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$. The $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$-module $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is finitely generated ($\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]), so by Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] (submodule $J$ whose image in $M/\mathfrak mM$ is everything) $J=\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, which is (c). Together with step 14, the admissible $A\supseteq A_0$ with residue field $F$, the $\lambda_j$ and the $\lambda'_i$ satisfy (a), (b), (c).
